explain.say: Put a metal spoon in hot soup and soon the handle is hot too. The heat has travelled along the solid metal by conduction.

faq.q: Why are metals good conductors of heat?
faq.a: Metals have free electrons that can move through the whole piece. They carry energy from the hot end to the cold end much faster than vibrating particles alone could.
asks: What makes a material conduct heat?

faq.q: Why do pans have plastic or wooden handles?
faq.a: Plastic and wood are thermal insulators: heat moves through them very slowly. So the pan heats your food while the handle stays cool enough to hold.
asks: Why aren't pan handles made of metal?

faq.q: Why does a wooden spoon stay cool?
faq.a: Wood has no free electrons and is full of tiny air pockets, so heat passes along it very slowly. The end in the soup gets hot, but the handle stays cool for a long time.
asks: Why use a wooden spoon for stirring?

faq.a: A thermal insulator is a material that heat passes through slowly, like wood, plastic, wool, foam or still air. We use insulators to keep heat in or out.
Silver conducts heat best of all the metals, with copper close behind. That is why some good saucepans have copper bases.
asks: What is the best heat conductor?

facts: Copper conducts heat more than a thousand times better than wood.
Silver is the best conductor of heat among the metals, with copper a close second.
